extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, advocates, employers, attorneys, and others who wish to submit comments on DHS/USCIS proposed immigration rules
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on U.S. Department of Homeland Security / U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services proposed immigration rules (how to submit, format requirements, and what substantive content is most helpful).

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to submit comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments can only be submitted online through the Federal Register document page by clicking "Submit a Public Comment." You may submit comments through the Federal eRulemaking Portal at regulations.gov, identified by the specific DHS Docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to submit comments by other channels; use the Federal Register page or regs.gov and select the correct DHS docket number so the comment is associated with the specific proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text box length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter your comment in the text box (must be fewer than 5,000 characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your comment exceeds 5,000 characters, use the upload option (PDF). Keep in mind the character limit when drafting in the on-site text field.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF submission format (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload your comment as a text-searchable PDF (PDF submission is recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PDFs are text-searchable (not image-only scans) so reviewers can search and process submissions. PDF upload avoids the 5,000-character box limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must be submitted in English, or an English translation must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting in another language, include a full English translation alongside the original so the comment will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference specific portion of the proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference a specific portion of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite the exact section, paragraph, or regulatory text you are addressing so reviewers can locate and evaluate the comment in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain reasons for recommended changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the reason for any recommended change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear rationale for suggested modifications rather than only stating agreement or opposition; tie reasons to facts, law, or policy consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support recommendations with data/information/authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Include data, information, or authority that support such recommended change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or cite empirical data, statistics, legal authority, studies, or other evidence to substantiate your claims and strengthen the comment's persuasiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite comments on all aspects and specific effects
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS invites all interested parties to submit written data, views, comments and arguments on all aspects of the proposed rule, and also invites comments relating to economic, environmental, or federalism effects that might result from the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider addressing wide-ranging impacts — not just the immediate regulatory text — including economic analysis, environmental consequences, and federalism implications where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited/invalid submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted by email or mail, or hand-delivered/couriered, will not be considered comments on the proposed rule and may not receive a response from DHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send comments by email, postal mail, or in person expecting them to be treated as official rulemaking comments; use the online portals specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of comments / bundling risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Any comments should be unique, as DHS may bundle any comments that are too similar to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting near-identical form letters without specific tailoring; individualized or substantive differences reduce the chance your comment will be bundled and increase the likelihood it receives separate consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify affected immigrant population
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the affected immigrant population (visa categories, status types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which visa categories, beneficiary groups, or status types would be affected by the proposed rule to help DHS assess scope and targeted impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include personal or family stories where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, relevant personal or family experiences to illustrate real-world effects, but tie anecdotes to factual claims or broader evidence when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific INA sections being implemented
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific INA sections being implemented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant Immigration and Nationality Act provisions to show how the proposed rule does or does not align with statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address economic impact (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address economic impact (employer/employee, US economy, immigrant communities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss direct and indirect economic consequences for employers, employees, broader U.S. economic effects, and impacts on immigrant communities; include data or economic analysis when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with Service Center processing capacity issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with Service Center processing capacity issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rule affects filing volumes or processing workflows, comment on whether USCIS service centers have capacity to implement the rule and how processing delays or backlogs might affect stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite peer-reviewed research on immigration impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite peer-reviewed research on immigration impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use peer-reviewed studies to substantiate claims about labor market effects, fiscal impacts, or other measurable consequences; provide full citations or links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note disparate impact on particular nationalities/regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note disparate impact on particular nationalities/regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether the rule would disproportionately affect people from specific countries or regions and provide evidence or examples to support disparate-impact claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address legal challenges to similar prior rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Address legal challenges to similar prior rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss past litigation against related rules, how courts ruled, and the implications for the current proposal; explain legal vulnerabilities or defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference federal court decisions (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference federal court decisions (DACA, TPS, public charge cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant case law (for example DACA, TPS, public charge decisions) to demonstrate judicial treatment of similar policies and to inform DHS's legal analysis.
